eldarUnifiedFolkWar.woodlandPoliticalOrganization:
CREATOR CANON (2026-11-22): Woodland Eldar primarily lived in self-governing, independent city-states, each with its own ruler and political interests; they were NOT organized as one prewar united state. Independence never meant refusing cooperation or union with other Woodland Eldar cities.

CREATOR REFINEMENT (2026-11-23): Six named major Woodland Eldar groupings are ALLIANCES, EACH of MULTIPLE independent city-states: Shadow Grove Clan, NightenVale, OakenMire, ForestStalkers, korntholl, and treewalkers. Cities retain political independence, distinctive rulers and interests inside their alliances; no single united Woodland state thereby exists. The women-only ley mother clan is the seventh listed Woodland group but its political form is still undecided. Royal Eldar constitute a SEPARATE centralized kingdom. Founding chronology, numbers of cities per alliance, internal governance, and relationships among alliances remain undecided.

LEY MOTHER KINGDOM (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23; supersedes prior open-organization caveat): The exclusively female Ley Mother Clan moved/expanded beyond an original settlement and founded its own kingdom comparatively less developed than the Royal Eldar, not than other Woodland Eldar. It is DISTINCT FROM the six independent-city alliances and from the Royal Eldar centralized kingdom. The clan's all-female composition is established; whether all subjects of its kingdom are female is NOT yet established. Founding date, territorial location, political institutions, culture, recruitment/population continuity, degree of development and relations with the other Eldar remain open.

CREATOR CLARIFICATION (2026-11-23): The Ley Mother Clan's kingdom is described as 'primitive' ONLY IN COMPARISON WITH THE ROYAL ELDAR KINGDOM. It is NOT primitive relative to the other Woodland Eldar city-states and alliances. The Ley Mothers are not established as backward, technologically inferior, or culturally less sophisticated than other Woodland Eldar; do not invent a woodland-to-Ley-Mother development gap. Royal Eldar development was substantially more dramatic overall, including its magical/technical and military technologies. The exact technologies, arts, government and relative strengths of the Ley Mother Kingdom are yet to be developed.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.woodlandIntercityRelations: CREATOR CANON (2026-11-22): Full-scale wars between Woodland Eldar city-states were VERY RARE. Most disputes were settled through diplomacy; occasional limited skirmishes and the odd duel also occurred. Cities could form alliances and act together when their interests aligned. Do not infer frequent internal wars or centuries of battlefield experience from their defense preparations.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.woodlandDistanceResistance: CREATOR CANON (2026-11-22): In GENERAL the farther a woodland city lay from the Royal Eldar heartland, the more fiercely it resisted the king in the Unification War. Many distant cities had CENTURIES to prepare and were unwilling to back down. This is a trend rather than an absolute rule: rulers' choices, city circumstances and political priorities could differ. Distinguish deep-forest military resistance from frontier food scarcity, which fell hardest on border Woodland Eldar.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.woodlandFirstConquestReactionNuance: CREATOR CANON (2026-11-22): No common woodland response followed the first treetop city's defeat. Some FARAWAY cities IMMEDIATELY forged alliances and stepped up long-standing defensive preparations; others mistakenly saw the conquest as a single limited resource grab and assumed the king would STOP once he acquired what he needed, not realizing he sought ALL woodland territories; still others immediately prepared to NEGOTIATE TERMS OF SUBJUGATION. These categories describe political tendencies, not fixed formal blocs, and their future decisions remain open.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.kingPostFirstConquestStrategy: CREATOR CANON (2026-11-22): Having won the first canopy city, the king selected CONSOLIDATION AND DIPLOMATIC OUTREACH before the next advance: establish royal administration in the captured city, secure the conquest, and open contact with neighboring Woodland Eldar city-states. This pause was a tactic in his existing plan of total subjugation, NOT a reversal to peaceful voluntary unification. Specific further conquests, messengers, negotiations, agreements and deployment details remain undecided.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.unificationWarToneDirection: CREATOR STORY DIRECTION (2026-11-22): The war should permit chaotic and exceptionally brutal episodes, potentially more violent at moments than familiar high-fantasy settings, while Orakana retains an overall dark, gritty but hopeful character. This is a narrative tone guideline; no particular atrocity or battle has been established solely by this instruction.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.secondToThirdAgeKingSurvival: CREATOR CORRECTION (2026-11-22): The two exceptionally long-lived rival Eldar half-brother kings are alive in the SECOND AGE material/mythology. This does NOT establish that either survives into the THIRD AGE. Their Third Age existence or absence, dates and causes of death if any, succession, and later kingdoms' fate are UNDECIDED. Do not call either king a Third Age or present-day ruler solely on the basis of Second Age accounts. 'Practically immortal' describes exceptional longevity, not confirmed immortality or deathlessness.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.woodlandIntraCitySolidarity: CREATOR CANON (2026-11-23): During the Unification War, Woodland Eldar in cities refusing royal subjugation generally viewed other woodland cities that willingly submitted to the Royal Eldar king as TRAITORS, and some might ACT on that judgment. Such action is possible, not guaranteed or yet specified. Within each city, inhabitants generally shared common goals and broadly UNDERSTOOD their own ruler's decision, whether resistance or submission. This denotes strong city-level solidarity, NOT unanimous opinion, unquestioning obedience, or universal approval of all royal policies. No specific attack, punitive raid or full-scale conflict between independent Woodland Eldar city-states is established by this statement. Any armed fighting between such cities would be INTERCITY or INTERSTATE warfare, not a civil war, because the Woodland Eldar had no single shared state.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.woodlandConflictTerminology: CREATOR CORRECTION (2026-11-23): Independent Woodland Eldar city-states did not form a single kingdom. Fighting between those different city-states is intercity/interstate warfare, NOT civil war. Each city-state generally understood and supported its own ruler's decision, while other cities that chose submission could be viewed as traitors. No specific hostilities are yet established; internal unrest within an individual city remains separate and undecided.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.firstCityRoyalSoldierReaction: CREATOR CANON (2026-11-23): After the first Woodland Eldar canopy city's defenders refused surrender and every defending soldier was killed, the Royal Eldar soldiers generally understood the deaths as UNAVOIDABLE CONSEQUENCES OF THE DEFENDERS' ACTIONS AND REFUSAL TO SUBMIT. Do not depict the army as collectively celebrating slaughter or as collectively mourning the deaths. This establishes the prevailing military interpretation of the first city's defeat; individual private reactions and later developments remain undecided.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.firstCityDefendersIgnorance: CREATOR CANON (2026-11-23): Defenders of the FIRST Woodland Eldar canopy city had NO KNOWLEDGE of what machines, siege weapons, magical contraptions and engineered capabilities the Royal Eldar army possessed or had developed. They did not understand the scale or nature of the force they were opposing when they resisted; their refusal to surrender must not be represented as a fully informed calculation against known siege technology. They had approximately two hours' notice of the army's approach, but NOT prior intelligence about its arsenal. Do not assume the exact moment the individual machines were revealed, their battlefield effects, or the defenders' reactions until specified.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.kingFirstConquestMixedReaction: CREATOR CANON (2026-11-23): The Royal Eldar king's response to the killing of EVERY defender at the first canopy city was a MIX OF (1) seeing their deaths as the foreseeable/unavoidable consequence of their refusal to submit, and (2) regarding the loss of Eldar warriors he had hoped to incorporate under his crown as regrettable or wasteful. This is not a claim he abandoned his objectives, disapproved of the royal military's operation, or knew in advance how every defender would die. Keep the king's nuanced reaction distinct from his soldiers' generally consequence-focused viewpoint.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.woodlandDevelopmentDuringRoyalRise: CREATOR CANON (2026-11-23): The independent Woodland Eldar cities were NOT technologically or magically static during the long prewar centuries and the Unification War. They continued making their OWN improvements and innovations, although the scale or pace of those advances was generally NOT AS DRASTIC as that of the Royal Eldar, especially in the royal army's remarkable siege engineering and military magic. Royal superiority at the FIRST canopy city is confirmed, but do not presume Woodland Eldar lacked ingenuity, never improved their defenses, or remained helpless elsewhere. The nature, pace, transfer between cities, adaptation after seeing royal machinery, and military impact of specific woodland developments remain UNDECIDED. It is not canon that royal technological superiority alone ensured future diplomatic submissions.
eldarUnifiedFolkWar.woodlandKnowledgeSharingByRelations: CREATOR CANON (2026-11-23): Whether Woodland Eldar city-states shared technological, magical, craft or military innovations depended MOSTLY ON THEIR RELATIONSHIP with the particular other city. Friendly or cooperative relationships could enable sharing; strained relations could limit it. This is not a blanket rule of universal open exchange or universal secrecy. Specific intercity relationships, their history, the kinds of discoveries shared, and their consequences in the Unification War remain TO BE DEVELOPED; creator plans to cover relations between city-states soon.

meta.livingWorldPrinciple: CREATOR DIRECTION (2026-11-23): Orakana should feel lived in, with people who have their own problems, relationships, ambitions, livelihoods and routines, not simply populations waiting for rulers, wars, legendary heroes or any predetermined protagonist. Blend mature political tensions, difficult daily life, curses, superstitions and folklore with Orakana's established magic, peoples and its existing creatures and wildlife; hunters may pursue those native creatures, with no Witcher 3-style monster imports. Inspiration from The Witcher is tonal and structural only; do not copy its proprietary characters, monsters, factions, plots or institutions. Each place and culture needs ordinary joys as well as suffering, and people continue making decisions when not observed. Concrete new customs, monsters, occupational institutions and historical incidents must be developed individually before being labeled established canon. CREATOR CORRECTION (2026-11-23): Witcher influence means the lived-in, morally complicated atmosphere, local curses, legends, rumours, superstitions and folklore, NOT Witcher 3-style monsters, copied monster concepts, or a Witcher-style monster-hunting profession/institution. Orakana already has a substantial native roster of creatures and wildlife that ordinary or skilled hunters may hunt, fear, study or coexist with as appropriate. Do not create a new Witcher-inspired monster category or assume every supernatural problem is a monster encounter. records.title: Orakana — Planetary Fundamentals
records.summary: A five-continent, magically alive world, approximately 50,000 km in diameter.
records.body:
Orakana is approximately 50,000 km in diameter and 157,080 km around. Its surface is 60% water and 40% land. A 24-hour day, 360-day year, and four roughly 90-day seasons govern the working calendar.

The older 13,400-km diameter, 42,000-km circumference and 71%-water model are superseded.

Everyday gravity, hydrology, weather, agriculture and biology behave as on Earth, by explicit creator decision. The world is magical; no further physical justification for familiar gravity is required unless the creator later requests one.

CREATOR WORLD-NAMING DECISION (2026-11-23): This planet and wider fantasy setting are officially named ORAKANA (former out-of-world development name: Eryndor). No planet geography, physical parameters or in-world civilization is modified by this naming choice.

MALEVOLENT ALTERNATIVE NAME — MALENKOR (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23): Some genuinely malevolent beings refer to this SAME PLANET as 'Malenkor'. Its official world/project name remains 'Orakana'. We have not decided the name's linguistic origin, meaning, why those beings use it, or which evil beings or groups know it. Do not presume all evil individuals share one belief system or universally use the same term.

MALENKOR ORIGIN UPDATE (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23; supersedes previous 'origin undecided' wording): Some inhabitants of Orakana began referring to their planet as MALENKOR during the Great Cataclysm that ended the First Age. Later, certain genuinely malevolent beings refused to return to the name Orakana. No universal use or particular etymology is established.

records.title: The Five Continents
records.summary: Avarra, Tharvorn, Sahrad, Orundel, Vaelora.
records.body:
Avarra contains Karak-Varn and the established Hammerfeld family and associated characters. No player-character starting location or mandatory narrative viewpoint is designated. Tharvorn is northern, Sahrad southern, Orundel eastern and Vaelora western. Every continent contains multiple peoples, states and traditions.

Twin Titans dry-land shares: Avarra 32%, Orundel 28%, Tharvorn 12%, Sahrad 12%, Vaelora 11%, islands and separate archipelagos 5%. No island territory should be counted twice. Coastlines, countries, mapping scales and precise intercontinental routes await further survey.

records.title: World Tone and Creative Rules
records.summary: Dark and gritty yet hopeful; no species is uniformly good or evil.
records.body:
Orakana contains exploitation, conquest, famine, prejudice and catastrophic loss, alongside friendship, celebration, scholarship, rescue and reform. Consequences matter. Fantasy-scale cities and heroes are allowed without requiring Earth-historical ceilings.

Long-lived peoples can have large families; birth rates are not silently adjusted. A person may devote a century to a craft or choose domestic life; cultures have distinct expectations. No single trait determines everyone in a people. The creator can revise accepted canon with explicit supersession and a retained change log.

LIVED-IN-WORLD PRINCIPLE (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23): All cultures and historical periods should portray ordinary inhabitants as people with self-directed lives: work, money, families and friendships, disagreements, celebrations, worries, local beliefs, health, ambitions and responsibilities. Politics, warfare, changing markets, monsters, magic and disasters should affect their everyday choices, but do not erase their independence or make every scene bleak. Include folklore, dangerous wilderness, monster-related problems, tough moral decisions and material hardship as appropriate to each region, inspired by the grounded texture of darker fantasy without copying another setting's specific content. Not every problem is solved by a protagonist or king; life advances offstage, with consequences. Specific new creatures, guilds, crises and individual stories remain unestablished until explicitly developed.

PROJECT DIRECTION (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23): Orakana is now primarily a self-standing, persistent worldbuilding passion project with the possibility of future fiction/books. There is no preselected player character or guaranteed hero. The Hammerfeld family, including Gloin, remains part of the world. Older Gloin gameplay is historical archive, not an active scene. Development must prioritize societies, individuals and consequences across Orakana rather than organizing history around one player-controlled viewpoint.

HISTORICAL DEPTH AND UNTOLD LIVES (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23): Build the world's systems and major events thoroughly before planning fiction; a finished war chronology does not preempt the innumerable personal experiences that occurred within it. Target approximately 85% or greater broad-setting development as an aspirational threshold for considering later stories, not a rigid numerical mandate.

CURSES AND FOLKLORE CLARIFICATION (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23): Draw tonal inspiration from dark fantasy folklore and curses, not Witcher-style creature species or special monster-hunter institutions. Orakana's existing diverse animals and creatures already provide hunting and wilderness danger. The world retains its own creature ecology, magic and cultural specificity.

records.title: Ages Versus Eras
records.summary: Worldwide Ages are not the same as continent-specific historical eras.
records.body:
Five worldwide Ages are recognized; the current one is the Fifth Age. Each civilization may name and subdivide historical time differently. The Second Age's Awakening, Wonder and Fire divisions are Avarran conventions, not mandatory world calendars.

The Era of Crowns in the Fifth Age has a documented year-numbering convention; the former Gloin roleplay date (Autumn Day 22, Year 3847) is archival and does not define a current protagonist or story start. Era of Crowns years must not automatically be counted from the global beginning of the Fifth Age.

records.title: Current World Population
records.summary: 2.0628 billion modeled residents across 28 numerical categories.
records.body:
The current sixfold planning census contains 2,062,800,000 modeled residents: Avarra 1,019,760,000; Tharvorn 171,000,000; Sahrad 282,222,000; Orundel 393,600,000; Vaelora 196,218,000. This replaces a 343.8-million draft.

Global Khazari 144 million, Eldar 108 million, Urakai 186 million, humans 960 million. The Seven Khazari Throne domains total 132 million and are INCLUDED within worldwide Khazari; Karak-Varn's 22.8 million are included within the Thrones. Drakari, Aelwyn and Living Mountains are not precisely enumerated.

This is a worldbuilding resimulation, not sudden births or a confirmed omniscient census. Metro-versus-domain boundaries need reconciliation.

CANON — AVARRAN SECOND-AGE BIRTH BOOM (2026-11-22): Across Avarra's peoples, the birth rate was at least 2× each people's ordinary baseline during the Era of Awakening (Second Age Years 1–321) and Era of Wonder (Years 322–1321), falling to approximately 1.5× baseline during the Era of Fire (Years 1322–1437). These are BIRTH-RATE multipliers, NOT multipliers of population totals; the population may keep rising after the birth rate falls. Khazari remained asleep for all of Awakening and awakened gradually during Years 322–488; they participate only from awakening onward, not during Years 1–321. This event is specific to Avarra and is not automatically imposed on the other continents. Ordinary baseline birth rates, previously established long lifespans, existing present-day population totals, and populations of other continents are NOT changed by this historical note. Population-size consequences, migration, mortality, disasters and subsequent-age demographics require a separate continuity audit.

CANON KHAZARI GEOGRAPHIC DISTRIBUTION (2026-11-22): The overwhelming majority of Khazari live in Avarra's Ironspine mountain system, the core homeland of the Seven Thrones. Only a few scattered pockets exist outside Avarra, primarily in some of the larger mountain ranges on other continents. Smaller Khazari settlements elsewhere within Avarra may exist, but no extensive overseas Khazari realm is implied. Exact percentages, population totals, and overseas settlement histories remain undecided pending demographic revision. The older 132-million Seven Thrones figure counts domain residents and must not automatically be equated to 132 million ethnic Khazari.

CANON KHAZARI DISTRIBUTION PERCENTAGES (2026-11-22): Of the WORLDWIDE Khazari population, 83% live in Avarra, including 74% living directly within the Ironspine mountain system and 9% elsewhere in surrounding Avarran regions; the remaining 17% live across other continents, principally in mountain ranges. These are percentages of the global Khazari population, NOT percentages of Avarra's population or of the 83% subgroup. Total worldwide Khazari headcount remains provisional pending demographic recalculation. Continuity review needed: the earlier description 'only a few scattered pockets outside Avarra' must be interpreted as geographically concentrated overseas settlements or revised, because 17% of the species is a significant minority. Do not invent overseas kingdoms or settlements without creator approval.

records.title: World Geography Awaiting Remapping
records.summary: A vast planet needs resurveyed roads, coastlines, maps and densities.
records.body:
The adopted 50,000-km world and the Twin Titans land allocation supersede earlier diagrams. Broad historical geography and relative regional relations survive, but many route lengths, schematics, old (x,y) throne coordinates and map-image scale bars are still provisional.

Exact river sources, political boundaries, coastlines, local population envelopes and long-distance voyage durations require later consistent mapping. Illustrative maps do not establish canon by themselves.

records.title: First Age
records.summary: Its length is unknown and no authentic contemporary records survive.
records.body:
Its duration is exactly 11,257 years (creator-corrected canon, 2026-11-22). CORRECTED CANON (2026-11-22): The lack of surviving pre-Great-Cataclysm records applies ONLY to the Khazari. Other peoples, including Eldar, humans and others, retained historical records from before the Cataclysm. The First Age is therefore NOT universally undocumented; surviving accounts may differ by culture and completeness. Old stories describe extraordinary prosperity, but their historical accuracy is unverified. It ended when the First Great Cataclysm destroyed or shattered moons. Lost moon-specific magics did not return.

Creator clarification (2026-11-21): Multiple moons collided, initiating the Great Cataclysm at the end of this Age; the collision trigger is established canon, not speculation.

CANON DURATION (2026-11-22, revised): The First Age lasted EXACTLY 11,257 years, superseding the previous 16,764-year figure. Its end is marked by the Great Cataclysm. Together with the Second Age (1,437 years) and Third Age (8,873 years), the first three ages total 21,567 years. Dates of the First Age Eldar Unification War and Golden Age remain undecided.

FIRST ELF DISAPPEARANCE (CANON, 2026-11-22): Approximately Year 2,200 of the First Age, the First Elf mysteriously disappeared one night, leaving the throne to his son. The disappearance's cause, circumstances, ultimate fate, and relationship to the Eldar Unification War remain UNDECIDED. Do NOT presume the son started the war immediately or that the war itself began in Year 2,200.

FIRST ELF'S HEIR (CANON, 2026-11-22): The First Elf's son was YOUNG AND INEXPERIENCED when he inherited the throne after the First Elf vanished around First Age Year 2,200. His exact age, abilities, policies, reign, and connection to the later Unification War are not yet established. Possible political consequences are suggestions, not canon.

FIRST ELF'S KINGDOM AT SUCCESSION (CANON, 2026-11-22): Around First Age Year 2,200, when the First Elf vanished and his young, inexperienced son inherited the throne, the Eldar kingdom was POWERFUL AND PROSPEROUS and occupied approximately ONE-FIFTH (20%) of Letharion Forest. It was NOT a failing or already fragmented kingdom at succession. Political distribution of the remaining ~four-fifths, and timing and motivations of the later Unification War, are undecided; do not presume the remaining territory was one bloc.

ORIGIN OF THE UNIFICATION AMBITION (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): After inheriting the powerful, prosperous Eldar kingdom covering about one-fifth of Letharion Forest around First Age Year 2,200, the First Elf's young, inexperienced son aspired to develop GREAT ELVEN MAGIC FORGES AND ARCANE TOWERS. Aesthetic/craftsmanship inspirations are Celebrimbor and the Elven smiths of Warhammer; this is inspiration, NOT automatic adoption of their powers or lore. He realized that even his prosperous kingdom lacked the MANPOWER and RESOURCES to achieve these grand projects. This realization CAUSED him to formulate and give his REASON/JUSTIFICATION FOR UNIFICATION: bringing the scattered Eldar together would supply the collective capacity to achieve his vision. This is the established origin of his unification rationale. The precise projects, magical mechanisms, diplomacy, timing and military steps remain undecided. Do not invent a prior conquest motive or claim the forges/towers were already built.

PREWAR TENSIONS AND INTENT (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): Long BEFORE the Unification War, the independent woodland Eldar and the prosperous royal Eldar kingdom already had tensions over the kingdom's increasingly intensive magical crafting, development, and resource use—roughly analogous to 'industrialization' as an out-of-world shorthand, NOT an in-world Eldar term or a modern industrial economy. The woodland Eldar opposed or resented this development. The royal kingdom's people were ALREADY ready to SUBJUGATE the forest's independent peoples. The young successor king did NOT consider peaceful overtures or negotiated voluntary unification: his ambitions for great magical forges and arcane towers, and the manpower/resource shortage, supplied PURPOSE and what the king and his people perceived as a CLAIM/JUSTIFICATION for the conquest they were already inclined to undertake. This is the royal rationale, not an objective legitimacy judgment. Exact outbreak date, campaigns, duration, forest cultures' native terminology, and war's devastation remain undecided.

OPENING STRATEGY OF THE ELDAR UNIFICATION WAR (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): Once ready, the First Elf's successor king secretly MOBILIZED HIS GREAT ARMY WITHIN THE ROYAL CAPITAL, concealing the assembled force from the independent woodland realms. Rather than launching an overt first attack, he PATIENTLY WAITED for the free/independent woodland Eldar to unknowingly and foolishly STRIKE THE FIRST BLOW. He anticipated and was prepared to exploit their aggression to give his planned subjugation the appearance of a justified response. The woodland realms genuinely strike first; their specific target, immediate provocation, whether the king manipulated a particular incident, war's start year, and military outcomes of the first engagement are UNDECIDED. Do not assume the woodland attack was fabricated or that the king ordered a false flag.

THE ROYAL SURVEYOR CARAVAN INCIDENT (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The woodland Eldar's genuine FIRST STRIKE was an ATTACK on a ROYAL SURVEYOR CARAVAN seeking LIMESTONE DEPOSITS needed for continued royal construction. The caravan carried a VERY IMPORTANT ELF (identity, role and fate not yet decided). It is DELIBERATELY UNRESOLVED whether the king knowingly sent the caravan, including its important passenger, as BAIT for the woodland Eldar; preserve this as a historical ambiguity, not an established secret plan. The king's great army had already been secretly mustered in the capital. Exact site, date, casualties, outcome for the passenger and immediate royal response are undecided.

SURVEYOR CARAVAN INCIDENT—OFFICIAL IDENTIFIED (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The important Elf travelling with the limestone-survey caravan was a HIGH-RANKING ROYAL BORDER/FRONTIER OFFICIAL in charge of the kingdom's frontier. He was accompanied by a SMALL NUMBER OF GUARDS, as was his normal practice. He KNEW WHAT HE WAS DOING OUT THERE, but the precise scope of his knowledge, including any knowledge of royal plans, is UNDECIDED. The official DIED in the woodland Eldar attack ('it's hard for a corpse to talk'). His death prevents him from explaining whether the expedition was bait or what the king intended. Preserve as an unresolved historical mystery whether the king deliberately exposed the official to danger; do not assert the official was a willing conspirator or deliberately sacrificed. The official's name, the guards' fates, and other casualties remain undecided.

IMMEDIATE ROYAL RETALIATION—MARCH ON FIRST WOODLAND CITY (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): After the woodland Eldar attacked the royal limestone-survey caravan and killed the high-ranking frontier official, AT LEAST ONE SURVIVOR rode to the royal capital. AS SOON AS THAT SURVIVOR ENTERED THE CAPITAL GATES, the king's already secretly mobilized great army IMMEDIATELY MOVED toward the FIRST KNOWN WOODLAND CITY. The king issued NO FORMAL DECLARATION OF WAR before the march. Do not insert a prior ultimatum, diplomatic attempt, delay or public proclamation. The city name, precise location, army size, whether the king personally accompanied it, how quickly the city was reached, and the outcome are UNDECIDED. Rapid mobilization may fuel later suspicion about the bait incident, but does NOT establish king's actual intent.

FIRST WOODLAND CITY'S DEFENSES (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The first known woodland city targeted by the king's army was a FOREST ROOFTOP/TREETOP CITY, built above ground amid the forest canopy. Its inhabitants received APPROXIMATELY A COUPLE OF HOURS' WARNING and had that much time to prepare defenses. HOWEVER, NOTHING THEY COULD HAVE PREPARED WOULD HAVE READIED THEM FOR WHAT THE KING'S ARMY HAD IN STORE. The nature of the royal army's unexpected tactics, weapons, magical capabilities, the battle's casualties and its outcome are NOT YET ESTABLISHED. Do not invent those details or presume the city was destroyed.

ROYAL ELDAR SIEGE ARSENAL AT FIRST WOODLAND CITY (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The royal army fields MIGHTY SIEGE WEAPONS: (1) BOLT THROWERS firing SEVEN-FOOT-LONG bolts at velocities too fast to be perceived even by the Eldar eye; (2) TREBUCHETS launching BALLS OF PURE ENERGY; and (3) SIEGE TOWERS tall enough to REACH THE FOREST CANOPY, with ARCANE MAGES ON EVERY FLOOR. These are existing military capabilities brought to the first treetop-city engagement. The precise mechanics, impact effects, spells, numbers, tactics, battle outcome, and casualties remain UNDECIDED. The king's ambitious great magical forges and arcane towers are still his broader construction vision; their completion is NOT implied by the existence of these siege engines. Do not silently import Warhammer or Tolkien magic rules.

ROYAL UNIFICATION POLICY AND SECRET CHILD (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): In the opening siege of the first woodland canopy city, the king intended to CAPTURE/PRESERVE rather than annihilate the city and its inhabitants, to demonstrate that his objective was UNIFICATION and to avoid undermining the MORALE of his own people. Separately, as one of his ways of attempting to bring the Eldar peoples together, the king FATHERED A CHILD WITH A WOODLAND ELDAR WOMAN WITHOUT HIS WIFE'S KNOWLEDGE. The woodland mother's identity, child's identity, birth timing and ultimate connection to the two near-immortal rival half-brother kings have NOT YET BEEN EXPLICITLY CONFIRMED: do not assume this child is the elder bastard-born rival king without asking the creator. The siege's exact result remains undecided.

ROYAL SIEGE SUPERIORITY AND PRIVATE LINEAGE REVEAL (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The royal army's advanced siege weapons made a CONVENTIONAL SIEGE OF THE WOODLAND TREETOP CITY EFFECTIVELY NULL AND VOID/OBSOLETE, helping the king overwhelm defenses while seeking to preserve the city and its people for unification. This does not yet specify actual battle result, damage, or casualties. The king's SECRET CHILD with a woodland Eldar woman IS CONFIRMED TO BE THE ELDER, BASTARD-BORN HALF-BROTHER of the two exceptionally long-lived rival kings known in later history. CRITICAL PRESENTATION RESTRICTION: The creator explicitly says 'DON'T CONNECT IT JUST YET': retain this identity as creator-confirmed backstage continuity, but DO NOT YET CONNECT/REVEAL the historical child to the later rival kingdoms in narrative exposition, public-facing in-world histories, or future plot until creator authorizes. The king's wife was unaware of the relationship. Preserve the separation between backstage canon and what characters/historians know.

FIRST WOODLAND CITY BATTLE—DEFENDERS' FATE (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The defenders of the first woodland canopy city STUBBORNLY REFUSED TO SURRENDER and FOUGHT against the overwhelmingly superior royal siege army. The fighting resulted in EVERY DEFENDING SOLDIER BEING KILLED. This was the king's first military victory in the war, though his goal was to preserve the city and unite the Eldar. Do NOT infer civilian massacre, destruction of the city, royal casualty numbers, or the precise fate of civilians: these remain UNDECIDED. 'Every soldier' refers to the city's defending soldiers, not every resident.

AFTERMATH OF FIRST WOODLAND CITY CONQUEST (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): Following the defeat and death of EVERY DEFENDING SOLDIER, the king OFFERED THE SURVIVING WOODLAND CIVILIANS CITIZENSHIP AND PROTECTION UNDER HIS CROWN. He also explicitly WARNED that ANY DISSIDENCE would be met with the IRON FIST OF THE ROYAL ARMY. Thus the king's unification policy combines incorporation and protection with uncompromising military repression of resistance. Do not infer that civilians accepted willingly, that there were no other civilian harms, or that this policy necessarily applied identically to every later city; those matters remain undecided.

WOODLAND REPUBLICS' REACTIONS TO FIRST CITY'S FALL (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): Following the royal conquest of the first treetop woodland city, the remaining independent woodland Eldar city-republics RESPONDED DIFFERENTLY. SOME ORGANIZED FORMAL ALLIANCES AND RESISTANCE against the king and his army. OTHERS BEGAN PLANNING DIPLOMATIC MEETINGS with the royal king to PEACEFULLY ENTER HIS KINGDOM. This establishes a divided woodland political response, not a unified front. The diplomatic meetings are PLANNED, not yet confirmed to have occurred; terms, results, participants, number of cities and eventual military campaigns are UNDECIDED. The king did not seek negotiated peaceful unification before the first strike, but some cities now proactively seek it.

PEACEFUL WOODLAND ACCESSION TERMS (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The royal king WELCOMED independent woodland Eldar cities seeking peaceful entry with FAVOURABLE TERMS and EQUAL CITIZENSHIP for their inhabitants. Each joining city was to be GOVERNED BY AN ELDAR NATIVE TO THAT CITY, personally SELECTED BY THE KING (local origin, crown-appointed authority). Cities could RETAIN THEIR WOODLAND STATUS, CANOPY CHARACTER, AND TRADITIONS, but were REQUIRED TO INCORPORATE THE ROYAL KINGDOM'S ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN AT GROUND LEVEL for GOVERNMENT BUILDINGS, ARCHIVES, and other royal institutions, as well as MAGIC FORGES, ARCANE TOWERS, and related royal magical developments. This is an explicit blend of cultural continuity with royal political control and required royal development. Do not assume exact construction pace, governor selection procedures beyond king's appointment, individual cities' compliance, or how these terms apply to resistant cities.

ROYAL MILITARY INTEGRATION IN CONQUERED CITIES (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): In CONQUERED woodland cities, the former independent city armies/guards were DISBANDED as autonomous formations; surviving members were RETRAINED TO ROYAL MILITARY PROTOCOL, then TRANSFERRED AND RESTATIONED ELSEWHERE in the kingdom. Their former city's guard posts were FILLED WITH ROYAL ARMY SOLDIERS stationed there instead. This prevents local independent armed forces while integrating former woodland troops into the royal military. EXCEPTION: At the FIRST attacked canopy city, EVERY defending soldier was killed, so there were no surviving defending soldiers from that battle to retrain; replacement garrisons may still be installed. Application of the same policy to cities that joined PEACEFULLY is NOT YET DECIDED; do not automatically extend it. Exact implementation details and royal ranks undecided.

MILITARY TERMS FOR PEACEFULLY INCORPORATED WOODLAND CITIES (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): Unlike forcibly conquered cities, woodland cities that JOINED THE KINGDOM PEACEFULLY RETAINED SOME LOCAL MILITARY/GUARD AUTHORITY. HIGH-RANKING SOLDIERS, including OFFICERS AND COMMANDERS, were required to be RETRAINED TO ROYAL MILITARY PROTOCOL. The BULK OF THE CITY GUARD REMAINED STATIONED IN ITS HOME CITY unless personnel SHOWED SIGNS OF DISOBEDIENCE, in which case the privilege of remaining could be withdrawn. Do not automatically apply the conquered-city policy of wholesale disbandment and replacement by royal troops to peaceful accession cities. Exact consequences of disobedience, command relationships and whether royal garrisons supplemented local guards are not yet established.

FIRST CONQUEST DATE (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The successor king's FIRST CONQUEST—the first woodland canopy city whose defenders fought to the last—occurred EXACTLY 1,086 YEARS AFTER HE TOOK THE THRONE. Since the First Elf disappeared and the son succeeded around First Age Year 2,200 (approximate), this places the conquest at approximately FIRST AGE YEAR 3,286, NOT an exact calendar date unless accession Year 2,200 is later fixed precisely. The 1,086-year interval is exact. This date refers to the FIRST CONQUEST, not the war's total duration or its eventual end. The caravan attack and immediate march precede the conquest, but their precise dates remain unestablished.

AUTHORITATIVE CHRONOLOGY CORRECTION (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): FIRST AGE YEAR 3,286 IS THE EXACT YEAR THE ELDAR UNIFICATION WAR BEGAN. This is NOT merely an approximate date for the first conquest. The war starts with the woodland Eldar's attack on the limestone-surveyor caravan and the king's immediate military response. The first treetop city is conquered in the opening campaign, but the exact date of its fall has NOT been established. The king's accession remains AROUND First Age Year 2,200, and the earlier 1,086-years-after-accession statement should be read as the intended interval leading to the outbreak/first conquest campaign, NOT as a reason to demote the explicit exact Year 3,286 war start. If the accession year or precise first-conquest date needs reconciliation, ask the creator rather than inventing an exact date. War end and duration remain undecided.

THE SUCCESSOR KING'S LONG DEVELOPMENTAL REIGN BEFORE WAR (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): Between taking the throne around First Age Year 2,200 and the exact outbreak of the Eldar Unification War in Year 3,286 (approximately 1,086 years), the First Elf's initially young and inexperienced son DID NOT REMAIN FOOLISH OR INCOMPETENT. He deliberately TOOK TIME TO LEARN THE ROLE OF KING and grew into a capable ruler. He built up the kingdom's MAGICAL ARCHITECTURE and TECHNOLOGY, MILITARY TECHNOLOGY, TRAINING and POWER, and made OVERALL IMPROVEMENTS to the kingdom. The powerful royal siege arsenal fielded in Year 3,286 arose from this long period of development. Do not portray him as an inept ruler or assume all 1,086 years were devoted exclusively to war preparation. The exact schedule and sequence of individual developments are not yet specified.

PRE-UNIFICATION ROYAL FLOURISHING (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): During the successor king's long prewar reign, roughly First Age Years 2,200–3,286, his subjects became INCREASINGLY DEVOTED TO HIM because he brought substantial WEALTH AND PROSPERITY through EXPANDING FOREIGN TRADE beyond Letharion Forest, including trade with DISTANT LANDS. Alongside royal advances in magical architecture, technology, military training and general development, this was a genuine PERIOD OF FLOURISHING AND DEVELOPMENT. It was explicitly NOT YET THE GREAT ELDAR GOLDEN AGE that followed eventual unification. Exact trade partners, routes, goods, trade volumes, institutional policies and chronology remain undecided; do not invent them as canon.

WOODLAND TRADE BENEFITS AND CARAVAN-GUARD COMPLACENCY (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): Independent woodland Eldar received SOME BENEFIT from the prosperous royal kingdom's foreign trade, but these benefits came at a COST TO RELATIONS WITH THE KING. Amid the royal kingdom's flourishing, SOME—not all—royal caravan guards grew LAZY/COMPLACENT. Woodland Eldar WATCHED FOR THESE PARTICULAR GUARDS ON THE CARAVANS and used their lapses as opportunities. Do not claim all royal troops lacked discipline: the well-trained main army and complacent subset of caravan guards coexist. Exact nature/frequency of woodland exploitation, whether these were raids or other acts, and any direct role in the specific limestone-surveyor incident are NOT YET CONFIRMED.

SURVEYOR CARAVAN ATTACK—WOODLAND INTELLIGENCE ERROR (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The limestone-surveyor caravan carrying the important royal official was NOT one of the caravans targeted because its guards were lazy or complacent. The woodland Eldar KNEW THE PASSENGER WAS IMPORTANT but DID NOT KNOW HIS ACTUAL ROLE. They believed KILLING OR CAPTURING HIM could potentially CRIPPLE A CRUCIAL PART OF THE KINGDOM. They did NOT realize he was 'JUST THE COMMANDER OF THE FRONTIER'—the high-ranking officer in charge of the kingdom's border/frontier. He died in the attack. Their intelligence mistake and speculative hoped-for strategic benefit must not be conflated with guard complacency. The king's possible use of the expedition as bait remains genuinely unresolved.

PREWAR WOODLAND DESPERATION AND ROYAL DISTRUST (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The frontier commander killed in the limestone surveyor caravan attack was EASY FOR THE KINGDOM TO REPLACE, contrary to the woodland attackers' hopes of crippling a crucial royal function. Independent woodland Eldar were ATTACKING ROYAL CARAVANS OUT OF DESPERATION, not merely for greed or sport. Royal Eldar viewed these caravan attacks as a THREAT TO THEIR PEACE, resulting in STRONG DISTRUST of the woodland Eldar. This distrust helped deepen the pre-existing divide. Do not invent the precise underlying causes of woodland desperation beyond what is established (worsening relations, royal expansion and development tensions); do not portray all woodland Eldar as uniformly supportive of attacks.

ROOT CAUSE OF WOODLAND BORDER DESPERATION: FOREST FOOD PRESSURE (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The independent woodland Eldar did NOT need the royal kingdom's industrial/construction resources such as iron, limestone, copper, etc. FOOD and other forest sustenance were different: as the royal Eldar kingdom's population SLOWLY INCREASED during its long prewar flourishing, royal Eldar took MORE AND MORE FOOD FROM LETHARION FOREST. This increasing pressure on shared forest food resources drove MANY BORDER WOODLAND ELDAR to DESPERATE MEASURES, explaining the desperate caravan attacks and worsening relations. Royal Eldar saw these attacks as a threat to their peace and developed strong distrust. This is a material ecological/subsistence conflict, not a contest for ore. Do not assume precise foods, harvesting mechanisms, famine levels, trade arrangements, deliberate royal starvation policies or universal woodland involvement without creator confirmation.

ROYAL KING'S AWARENESS OF FOOD PRESSURE (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The successor king PERSONALLY ORDERED hunting and gathering in Letharion Forest to supply his growing royal population. However, he DID NOT REALIZE HOW SEVERE the impact on the woodland Eldar, particularly the border communities, had become. His orders contributed to the food pressures behind woodland desperation and caravan attacks, but do NOT portray him as knowingly or deliberately trying to starve the woodland Eldar. The precise nature of information reaching him, possible advisers' warnings, and later realization are not yet established.

PREWAR WOODLAND ELDAR PRIDE AND DIPLOMATIC RELUCTANCE (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): At this stage the independent woodland Eldar were STUBBORN and viewed the royal Eldar as HAUGHTY, PRETENTIOUS, and OVERLY CONCERNED WITH STATUS AND FORMALITY (creator's 'posh/uptight' meaning). Because of that attitude, woodland Eldar REFUSED TO INITIATE CONVERSATION WITH ROYAL ELDAR; they would speak to royal Eldar ONLY IF THE ROYAL ELDAR APPROACHED FIRST. This reluctance obstructed direct communication of legitimate grievances, including worsening food pressures. Do not treat this as a permanent universal trait of all woodland Eldar across every era, or invent specific failed embassies, negotiations or warnings. King ordered forest hunting/gathering without understanding full woodland hardship.

MUTUAL ROYAL–WOODLAND ELDAR PREJUDICE GRADIENT (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): Inspired loosely by Caesar's observation about peoples distant from luxury/civilization, BOTH royal and independent woodland Eldar held cultural prejudices about the other. Woodland Eldar could regard royal Eldar as softened by wealth, comfort, refinement and elaborate civilization, while royal Eldar could regard woodland Eldar as provincial, stubborn and resistant to progress. The FURTHER AWAY from the royal kingdom a woodland Eldar community was, the STRONGER these opinions became ON BOTH SIDES. Border communities tended to have more direct interaction and relatively weaker cultural estrangement; distant communities and royal perceptions of them were more polarized. These are in-world mutual perceptions, NOT objective assessments of either group's courage or capability. This gradient is distinct from the strongest material food-pressure effects on woodland border communities. Do not imply universal uniform attitudes or make specific distant settlements' politics canon without creator approval.

WOODLAND ELDAR CITY-STATES & INTERCITY PEACE (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): Before the Unification War, Woodland Eldar settlements were primarily INDEPENDENT CITY-STATES, each governed by its own ruler. They were protective of their sovereignty without rejecting alliances or cooperation with other Woodland Eldar cities. FULL-SCALE WAR between woodland city-states was VERY RARE: they normally settled rivalries through DIPLOMACY, with occasional LIMITED SKIRMISHES and the odd DUEL. Do not portray them as a pre-existing unitary confederation or as habitually fighting large wars against one another.

DEEP-WOODLAND RESISTANCE GRADIENT (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): During the king's Unification War, the more distant a Woodland Eldar city was from the Royal Eldar heartland, the more FIERCELY it GENERALLY resisted conquest. The distant settlements had CENTURIES to prepare for conflict and were unwilling to surrender; nevertheless rulers and particular circumstances could produce exceptions. This long-term military preparedness does not establish continuous combat experience or frequent woodland-on-woodland wars. It also must not be confused with the greater PREWAR FOOD PRESSURE suffered by woodland communities closest to the royal frontier.

THREE DIFFERENT EARLY WOODLAND RESPONSES (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): News of the first canopy city's fall did NOT yield a unified response. SOME DISTANT CITIES IMMEDIATELY MADE ALLIANCES and escalated their existing defense preparations. OTHERS believed the king only needed a particular city or natural resources and would STOP once he obtained them; they failed to grasp that he intended TOTAL SUBJUGATION OF THE WOODLAND CITIES. STILL OTHERS IMMEDIATELY PREPARED FOR TALKS about terms of submission. These descriptions are broad tendencies, not an exhaustive immutable classification of city-states; their subsequent choices and the specific cities involved remain undecided.

KING'S POST-CONQUEST CONSOLIDATION (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): After the first canopy city's conquest, the king CHOSE TO PAUSE FURTHER ADVANCE, CONSOLIDATE and ESTABLISH ROYAL ADMINISTRATION of the captured city, then BEGIN DIPLOMATIC CONTACT with neighboring woodland city-states. He did NOT abandon his objective of bringing every woodland territory under royal authority. The details and outcomes of the subsequent talks and the timing of his next campaign are NOT YET DECIDED. Do not invent an ultimatum, ambassadors' specific negotiating powers, or automatically assume that contacted rulers accepted.

UNIFICATION WAR'S INTENDED SEVERITY (CREATOR STORY DIRECTION, 2026-11-22): The conflict may contain periods of extraordinary brutality, fierce resistance, unpredictable chaos and moments of mercy, within the wider setting's dark, gritty yet hopeful tone. No individual massacre, siege method or atrocity is confirmed by this tonal direction alone.

WOODLAND CITIES' LOYALTY AND BETRAYAL PERCEPTIONS (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23): Woodland Eldar cities making different decisions about royal conquest could become bitterly divided. Residents of cities that RESISTED would generally consider voluntarily SUBMITTING woodland cities TRAITORS, with the possibility that some might act against them. At the same time, each Woodland Eldar city generally had SHARED GOALS AMONG ITS OWN PEOPLE, who mostly UNDERSTOOD why their ruler chose to resist or negotiate subjugation. Therefore, sharp intercity hostility could coexist with substantial unity within each city. Internal support is a tendency, NOT total unanimity or uncritical approval; dissent remains possible. Specific retaliatory acts or warfare between independent Woodland Eldar city-states are NOT yet established. If such clashes occurred they would be intercity/interstate conflicts, NOT civil war, since the Woodland Eldar had no common state. Internal unrest within any individual city-state is a separate unresolved possibility.

ROYAL SOLDIERS' RESPONSE TO THE FIRST CANOPY CITY (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23): After the first Woodland Eldar canopy city's defenders refused to surrender and every defending soldier was killed, the Royal Eldar soldiers generally viewed the outcome as the UNAVOIDABLE CONSEQUENCES of the defenders' own choices and resistance. They understood the result as a consequence of refusing royal authority, NOT as a reason for collective celebration of killing or a cause for collective regret. Individual soldiers could have private feelings, but those are not yet established. This describes the first conquest's prevailing military reaction only; do not automatically generalize it to every later battle or create specific celebrations, protests or atrocities without creator direction.

FIRST CITY DEFENDERS' LACK OF KNOWLEDGE AND KING'S MIXED RESPONSE (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23): The defenders of the FIRST woodland canopy city had NO IDEA what siege machinery, magical weapons or engineered contraptions the ROYAL ELDAR ARMY had created or could deploy. Having approximately two hours to prepare for the approaching army did NOT grant them meaningful advance intelligence about its arsenal. Their refusal to surrender and their deaths in the battle must not be described as a fully informed decision against weapons whose capabilities they knew. This is distinct from the ROYAL SOLDIERS' general belief that resistance brought unavoidable consequences. The KING himself held a MIXED VIEW: he too saw the defenders' deaths as consequences of their resistance, but also considered the destruction of so many Eldar warriors a regretful WASTE, given his desire to bring the woodland population under royal rule rather than annihilate it. The precise battlefield sequence, siege machinery's effects, defenders' immediate reactions, royal casualties and city damage remain undecided. Do not infer the king changed his unification policy.

WOODLAND ELDAR INDEPENDENT ADVANCEMENT (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23): While the Royal Eldar under their king pursued dramatic advances in magical engineering, military machines and other development, independent WOODLAND ELDAR CITY-STATES WERE ALSO DEVELOPING AND IMPROVING THEIR OWN TECHNOLOGY, CRAFT, MAGIC AND CAPABILITIES. Their advances were generally LESS DRASTIC than those of the Royal Eldar but were REAL and continuous; they must not be portrayed as unchanged for centuries. The first canopy city's defenders' ignorance of the PARTICULAR UNFAMILIAR ROYAL SIEGE MACHINES remains canon, and the royal army's major advantage in that opening conquest is retained. This does not imply woodland inventions were useless or that later woodland cities could not adjust. Exact woodland inventions, adoption rates, military applications, responses to the royal arsenal, and the extent to which other woodland rulers would negotiate submission from fear or other motives are all OPEN.

WOODLAND ELDAR KNOWLEDGE EXCHANGE (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23): Sharing inventions, techniques and magical or military discoveries between independent Woodland Eldar city-states depended MOSTLY on the particular RELATIONSHIP between the cities involved. No blanket system of universal sharing or universal secrecy is established. Do not assume all cities had access to identical innovations. The specific friendships, rivalries, alliances, exchanges and withheld discoveries are OPEN and will be developed when their intercity relations are explored.

records.title: First Great Cataclysm
records.summary: Multiple moons collided, triggering the Great Cataclysm and ending the First Age.
records.body:
Multiple moons collided, initiating the Great Cataclysm that ended the First Age and overturned the world's civilizations and lunar magical order. Destroyed source-moons permanently ended their associated magical disciplines; fragments of some shattered bodies became new moons and sources of new magic. The initiating multiple-moon collisions are established canon. Exact participating moon count, collision sequence, wider cascade and subsequent astronomical details remain open.

CREATOR REOPENED FOR EDITING (2026-11-21): All aspects of the Great Cataclysm, including the multiple-moon collision trigger, sequence, extent, lunar magic consequences and dating, may be reconsidered. The above describes the previous established version, preserved for comparison; do not treat the collision mechanism as newly immutable canon while revisions are underway.

CREATOR'S NEW HISTORICAL DIRECTION (2026-11-21; under development): The First Throne was a vast subterranean Khazari empire centered in the Ironspine Mountains. The inland sea enclosed by the mountain ring is linked to a mysterious magical harness or power system that the First Throne learned to use. Its exploitation precipitated the Great Cataclysm and the empire's fall. The catastrophe, the Silence Below and the eastern mine are to have connected histories; precise mechanisms, sequence, dates, and nature of the mine connection are deliberately undecided. The previously established multiple-moon collision scenario is under revision: do not assert whether collisions caused the catastrophe or were caused by the harness until decided. This is a working historical direction, not license to invent missing details.

CREATOR CONFIRMATION (2026-11-21): The First Throne discovered an extraordinary naturally occurring magical power beneath the Ironspine Mountains, then engineered and constructed a vast artificial harness to exploit it. The inland sea is connected to this system, but its precise role (source, regulator, consequence, or other) remains undecided. Exploitation of the system ultimately triggered the Great Cataclysm and contributed to the empire's fall. The failure mechanism, lunar collision relationship, and eastern mine/Silence Below connection remain open; do not invent these details.

CREATOR CONFIRMATION (2026-11-21): The inland sea BOTH contains and naturally regulates the extraordinary magical power. Without any artificial harness it can accomplish wondrous things but remains unpredictable. The First Throne's Khazari sought to control and exploit that power; dwarven greed for mastery and power is a thematic cause of their overreach. The artificial harness's interference with natural regulation precipitated the Great Cataclysm and the empire's fall. Greed is an imperial motivation, not a universal moral property of all Khazari. Exact engineering, failure mechanism, moon collisions and mine/Silence Below linkage remain open.

CREATOR HISTORICAL DIRECTION (2026-11-21): The eastern mine's ancient deeper workings are components of the First Throne's immense magical harness connected to the inland sea; this is why their unusual engineering attracts investigation. An immensely powerful Balrog-like (analogy only, not a Tolkien Balrog) being was SENT into the depths to stop the machine and is now locked/sealed there. The being's sender, origin, nature, alignment, actions, exact sealing agent, and whether the harness was fully stopped remain undecided. Preserve the difference between being sent to stop the machine and being responsible for causing the Cataclysm. Present-day investigation does not revive erased Gloin gameplay.

CREATOR REFINEMENT (2026-11-21): The powerful sealed being was sent not merely to stop the First Throne's harness, but to STOP AND PUNISH the dwarven empire itself for its greed and overreach in trying to control the inland sea's power. This is a punitive intervention against the First Throne's actions, with an atmosphere reminiscent of Tolkien's Balrog but an original Orakana being, not literally a Balrog. The sender, mandate's exact scope, creature's identity, when it arrived, deeds, and sealing remain open. Do not reduce its mission to a technical machine shutdown or assume all Khazari were guilty.

CREATOR CANON CLARIFICATION (2026-11-21): The First Throne is ALREADY FORGOTTEN by the Second Age for magical reasons tied to the Great Cataclysm. Second Age Khazari do not consciously know of the First Throne or found the Seven Thrones as deliberate successors to it. Shared ancestral heritage, surviving structures, traditions and machinery may persist without remembered provenance. The exact memory-erasure mechanism, geographic scope, exceptions, persistence, and whether anyone retained partial knowledge remain UNDECIDED. Previous suggestions that early Second Age founders knowingly preserve First Throne laws, records, dynastic claims or direct political succession are not canon.

CREATOR CONFIRMATION (2026-11-21): The Khazari awoke gradually across a 167-year span at the START of the Second Age's second Avarran era, the Era of Wonder: Second Age Years 322–488 inclusive (167 years). They had slept beneath the mountains since the Great Cataclysm, and the First Throne was magically forgotten. The First Throne kept very few conventional written documents because it developed an advanced magical method of writing OR of storing information directly in people's minds, rendering routine written documentation obsolete except for special cases; surviving ordinary written documents would mainly be very old, predating the system, or special-purpose. Whether the actual mechanism is magical writing, mind-storage or a hybrid remains UNDECIDED. Do not canonize a particular storage medium or how it failed. Earlier early-Second-Age active Khazari rebuilding narratives must be revised to reflect the slumber.

CREATOR PROPOSAL (2026-11-21, tentative and revisable): First Throne magical information technology may have originated as TWO distinct disciplines—magical writing and magical memory/storage in minds—subsequently fused into an integrated knowledge-preservation system. One or both source magics, or only the fusion technique, may have been lost during the Great Cataclysm and magical forgetting. Exact survival/loss pattern is NOT decided. Assistant working labels 'Runic Inscription', 'Mindbinding' and 'Living Archive', and any detailed capabilities, are illustrative proposals only, not canon. Avoid choosing a loss outcome without creator confirmation.

CREATOR DECISION (2026-11-21): Canon: First Throne developed TWO distinct magical information disciplines, magical writing and magical memory, then FUSED them into the advanced archival system that rendered conventional documents largely obsolete. The FUSION TECHNIQUE WAS LOST following the First Throne's fall/Cataclysm. Preserve BOTH previously discussed historical possibilities: some knowledge may be lost with dead living custodians, while ancient external magical archives may remain intact yet inaccessible because the fusion cannot be reproduced. The independent disciplines may have survived in whole, fragmentary or altered form; their exact survival and mechanics are not yet established. Working names 'Runic Inscription', 'Mindbinding' and 'Living Archive' remain noncanonical placeholders.

CREATOR RESOLUTION (2026-11-21): The First Throne's fused magical-writing/magical-memory technique was lost SPECIFICALLY THROUGH THE MAGICAL FORGETTING, not because the Great Cataclysm physically destroyed the technique or its archival substrates. The Cataclysm and slumber remain connected historical events; exact mechanics of forgetting and which independent disciplines survived remain undecided. Previously speculative alternative that the Cataclysm itself severed the fusion is superseded.

CREATOR CANON CORRECTION (2026-11-21): First Throne archival systems must remain ACCESSIBLE in principle to Khazari without personal magical ability: non-magical dwarves existed even in the First Age, so the civilization's information infrastructure was not restricted to mage users. Distinguish access/use from ability to invent, fuse, repair, reproduce, or fully understand the two original magical disciplines. The magical forgetting erased knowledge of the writing-memory fusion, but did NOT categorically render all surviving archives unreadable or inaccessible. Some archives may remain hidden, sealed, damaged, restricted, or difficult to understand; exact non-magical interface and operating rules undecided. Supersedes earlier speculation that all intact archives were inaccessible solely because fusion knowledge was lost.

LINGUISTIC CONSEQUENCE — MALENKOR (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-23): During the Great Cataclysm that ended the First Age, some people/beings began calling Orakana 'Malenkor'. Some genuinely malevolent beings later deliberately kept that name instead of returning to 'Orakana'. This naming history does NOT decide the Cataclysm's debated magical mechanics, exact sequence, or the full list of who used either name.

records.title: The Second Age — Avarran Chronology
records.summary: Exactly 1,437 years worldwide, divided in Avarran histories into Awakening (1–321), Wonder (322–1,321) and Fire (1,322–1,437).
records.body:
Exactly 1,437 years worldwide, divided in Avarran histories into Awakening (1–321), Wonder (322–1,321) and Fire (1,322–1,437). Other continents may use different names, eras and date boundaries.

CREATOR CANON CLARIFICATION (2026-11-21): The First Throne is ALREADY FORGOTTEN by the Second Age for magical reasons tied to the Great Cataclysm. Second Age Khazari do not consciously know of the First Throne or found the Seven Thrones as deliberate successors to it. Shared ancestral heritage, surviving structures, traditions and machinery may persist without remembered provenance. The exact memory-erasure mechanism, geographic scope, exceptions, persistence, and whether anyone retained partial knowledge remain UNDECIDED. Previous suggestions that early Second Age founders knowingly preserve First Throne laws, records, dynastic claims or direct political succession are not canon.

CREATOR CANON DIRECTION (2026-11-21): Throughout most of the Second Age, Khazari/dwarven societies were largely isolated; other peoples knew little or nothing reliable about them. Significant outside awareness/contact did not develop until the late Second Age. This does not imply low populations, technological backwardness, total absence of isolated individual contacts, or an exact year for broader contact. The proposed early/middle/late phases are illustrative, not locked historical events.

CREATOR NEW LORE (2026-11-21): In addition to magical forgetting of the First Throne, the Khazari/dwarves slept beneath the mountains after the Great Cataclysm until the 'second era'. Context suggests the second Avarran era of the Second Age (Era of Wonder, Years 322–1321), but this exact interpretation and wake-up year are not yet explicitly confirmed. The slumber's mechanism, whether all dwarves were affected, duration and pattern of awakening, and what memories survived remain undecided. This supersedes any portrayal of extensive active Khazari rebuilding during the early Second Age.

CREATOR CONFIRMATION (2026-11-21): The Khazari awoke gradually across a 167-year span at the START of the Second Age's second Avarran era, the Era of Wonder: Second Age Years 322–488 inclusive (167 years). They had slept beneath the mountains since the Great Cataclysm, and the First Throne was magically forgotten. The First Throne kept very few conventional written documents because it developed an advanced magical method of writing OR of storing information directly in people's minds, rendering routine written documentation obsolete except for special cases; surviving ordinary written documents would mainly be very old, predating the system, or special-purpose. Whether the actual mechanism is magical writing, mind-storage or a hybrid remains UNDECIDED. Do not canonize a particular storage medium or how it failed. Earlier early-Second-Age active Khazari rebuilding narratives must be revised to reflect the slumber.

CANON — AVARRAN SECOND-AGE BIRTH BOOM (2026-11-22): Across Avarra's peoples, the birth rate was at least 2× each people's ordinary baseline during the Era of Awakening (Second Age Years 1–321) and Era of Wonder (Years 322–1321), falling to approximately 1.5× baseline during the Era of Fire (Years 1322–1437). These are BIRTH-RATE multipliers, NOT multipliers of population totals; the population may keep rising after the birth rate falls. Khazari remained asleep for all of Awakening and awakened gradually during Years 322–488; they participate only from awakening onward, not during Years 1–321. This event is specific to Avarra and is not automatically imposed on the other continents. Ordinary baseline birth rates, previously established long lifespans, existing present-day population totals, and populations of other continents are NOT changed by this historical note. Population-size consequences, migration, mortality, disasters and subsequent-age demographics require a separate continuity audit.

SECOND-TO-THIRD AGE KING SURVIVAL CORRECTION (CREATOR CANON, 2026-11-22): The two exceptionally long-lived half-brother Eldar kings featured as LIVING rulers in SECOND AGE mythology and historical accounts. The creator explicitly clarified that this DOES NOT MEAN THEY REMAIN ALIVE IN THE THIRD AGE. Survival, deaths, reign endings, successors and the fate of their kingdoms after the Second Age are OPEN and must never be guessed. Their 'practically immortal' description is NOT a guarantee of living indefinitely, and the existence of the kings in one age is not proof of continued personal rule in any subsequent age. Do not label either a Third Age or present-day king without a further creator decision.

records.title: Era of Awakening
records.summary: Years 1–321 in Avarran chronology.
records.body:
Years 1–321 in Avarran chronology. Peoples rebuilt after lunar disruption, learned to support their societies through mundane agriculture, engineering, records and sanitation alongside surviving magic. Unequal recovery, famine, exploitation and reform all occurred.

CREATOR'S NEW HISTORICAL DIRECTION (2026-11-21; under development): The First Throne was a vast subterranean Khazari empire centered in the Ironspine Mountains. The inland sea enclosed by the mountain ring is linked to a mysterious magical harness or power system that the First Throne learned to use. Its exploitation precipitated the Great Cataclysm and the empire's fall. The catastrophe, the Silence Below and the eastern mine are to have connected histories; precise mechanisms, sequence, dates, and nature of the mine connection are deliberately undecided. The previously established multiple-moon collision scenario is under revision: do not assert whether collisions caused the catastrophe or were caused by the harness until decided. This is a working historical direction, not license to invent missing details.

CREATOR CONFIRMATION (2026-11-21): The First Throne discovered an extraordinary naturally occurring magical power beneath the Ironspine Mountains, then engineered and constructed a vast artificial harness to exploit it. The inland sea is connected to this system, but its precise role (source, regulator, consequence, or other) remains undecided. Exploitation of the system ultimately triggered the Great Cataclysm and contributed to the empire's fall. The failure mechanism, lunar collision relationship, and eastern mine/Silence Below connection remain open; do not invent these details.

CREATOR CONFIRMATION (2026-11-21): The inland sea BOTH contains and naturally regulates the extraordinary magical power. Without any artificial harness it can accomplish wondrous things but remains unpredictable. The First Throne's Khazari sought to control and exploit that power; dwarven greed for mastery and power is a thematic cause of their overreach. The artificial harness's interference with natural regulation precipitated the Great Cataclysm and the empire's fall. Greed is an imperial motivation, not a universal moral property of all Khazari. Exact engineering, failure mechanism, moon collisions and mine/Silence Below linkage remain open.

CREATOR CONFIRMATION (2026-11-21): The eastern mine extends far deeper than its previously documented six public and nine private-survey levels; these are only upper portions of a far larger ancient First Throne installation. Every dwarven hold has a deep connection/passage leading toward a shared central convergence where the Great Harness machinery meets, associated with the magical inland sea. Knowledge is uneven: some holds/rulers know of the passages or their purpose, others know only fragments, and others are unaware.
