records.title: Creative Direction — Persistent World and Future Stories
records.summary: Orakana is an independent, evolving passion project that may become a book series. No protagonist or player character is predetermined.
records.body:
CREATOR DECISION (2026-11-23)

ORAKANA'S PURPOSE: The setting is a long-term passion project built through persistent world history, autonomous cultures and characters, political and social developments, ordinary daily lives, evolving magic, creatures, mystery and consequences. The creator may eventually develop one or multiple novels or series; that possibility is not a book contract, published work or canon story arc.

NO DEFAULT PLAYER CHARACTER OR HERO: No roleplaying player character, default narrative protagonist, chosen-one destiny or mandated campaign starting scene is currently assigned. The world persists even without an observer or player. Future fiction can follow different people, places and eras. A future interactive campaign, if one is ever started, would establish its character and starting conditions at that time.

GLOIN AND FAMILY: Gloin Hammerfeld remains an established resident of Karak-Varn, and his established Hammerfeld family and associates remain part of the world. Their relationships, ages and backgrounds are preserved subject to separate continuity checks. They may be featured in future stories but are not obligated to be central characters. Gloin's possible First Throne ancestry is genuinely undecided. No person automatically receives player-driven discoveries or powers.

OLDER ROLEPLAY: Gloin's former interactive Day 19–22 narrative was already retired from active canon on 2026-11-21. Preserve it as a noncanonical historical archive only; do not falsely say its final scene is currently paused, or invent that the old appointments, inventory and discoveries still stand.

AUTHORING RULE: Use clear canon, working, unresolved and archival labels. Let cultures, communities, and individual lives continue independently; never force changes to existing mysteries or predetermine characters' fates merely to fill a plot outline.

WORLDBUILDING BEFORE STORYTELLING (CREATOR DIRECTION, 2026-11-23): The creator wants Orakana developed to an aspirational ~85% MINIMUM of broad worldbuilding completeness before even considering actual book stories. This is a planning aspiration, not a literal scientifically measurable global percentage or a guarantee every detail must be decided. Prioritize filling large world-system gaps: historical sequences, political relations, cross-continental civilizations, societies and cultures, geography, magic, ecology, economy, faith, daily lives and long-term consequences. Do not prematurely select a protagonist, book chronology, plot or character arc. Large histories can be thoroughly established, including the complete major course of the Eldar Unification War, while still allowing countless future stories set during them. Distinguish MACROHISTORY (widely known causes, major events, geopolitics, outcomes, and consequences) from MICROSTORIES (particular ordinary people, eyewitness encounters, private motives and unrecorded local events). Preserve freedom for later narratives without deliberately leaving major shared history incoherent or inventing every personal storyline in advance.

OFFICIAL WORLD NAME (2026-11-23): The creator officially renamed the project WORLD to ORAKANA, replacing the former working name ERYNDOR. This is a real-world authoring/name decision, NOT an in-world event. All established geography, continents, peoples, histories, and unresolved mysteries are carried over without changes. Historical source documents retain their original names for provenance. This record's technical ID is deliberately unchanged to preserve internal links.

The Ley Mothers are not established as backward, technologically inferior, or culturally less sophisticated than other Woodland Eldar; do not invent a woodland-to-Ley-Mother development gap. records.body:
CREATOR CANON — ORIGIN OF MALENKOR (2026-11-23): During the Great Cataclysm at the END OF THE FIRST AGE, SOME PEOPLE/BEINGS began calling the planet 'Malenkor' rather than 'Orakana'. The name was a historical response to the catastrophe, NOT exclusively a term invented by inherently evil beings. After the Cataclysm, while Orakana continued or returned as the ordinary name, certain genuinely malevolent beings REFUSED to go back to calling the world Orakana and continued using Malenkor across subsequent ages. Their adoption/retention does NOT prove those beings all created the name, were all active during the Cataclysm, belong to one faction, or have a shared explanation for choosing it. Exact first speakers, word meaning/etymology, regional diffusion, which ordinary communities used it and for how long, and which particular evil groups preserved it are UNDECIDED. The Great Cataclysm's contested magical cause and mechanics remain undecided and must not be fixed by this naming history.

Orakana and Malenkor ALWAYS refer to the SAME PLANET. The latter's origin was not necessarily malevolent, even if evil beings became known for keeping it. No specific gods, factions, places, invented etymologies or catastrophe mechanics are established by the naming decision. Earlier blanket statements that Malenkor's era of origin was unknown are superseded: its emergence DURING the Great Cataclysm is now canon.
